title: Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities 2026: Apply for International Tenders, Consulting Contracts and Global Health Procurement Opportunities
summary: About the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria The Global Fund is an international financing partnership dedicated to accelerating progress against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria while supporting stronger and more resilient health systems. Rather than directly implementing most country programs itself, the Global Fund finances programs that are implemented through its partners and Principal Recipients. This distinction is important when reviewing its business opportunities. The organization s Business Consultancy Opportunities page primarily covers procurement undertaken by the Global Fund itself, particularly requirements of its Secretariat. Principal Recipients administering Global Fund grants may conduct their own procurement processes separately in accordance with applicable grant requirements. The Global Fund s procurement activities are intended to support its organizational operations while helping ensure that resources ultimately contribute to effective global health interventions. What Are Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities? The opportunities published through the platform are essentially competitive procurement exercises . Depending on the requirement, the Global Fund may seek proposals from: Individual consultants Consultancy firms Professional service providers Companies Contractors Suppliers Manufacturers Technical organizations Research organizations Specialist agencies Procurement service providers Other qualified entities The Global Fund s Procurement Policy defines a supplier broadly as an external entity that may include an organization, individual contractor or service provider supplying goods, services or other support. Consequently, applicants should not assume that every opportunity is intended for an individual consultant. Some tenders may require established companies or organizations capable of delivering substantial contracts. What Types of Opportunities May Be Available? The exact opportunities change throughout the year. Potential procurement areas can include professional and technical services associated with the Global Fund s operations and mission. Depending on organizational requirements, opportunities may potentially cover areas such as: Global health consulting HIV-related technical services Tuberculosis programs and expertise Malaria-related technical services Health-system strengthening Procurement and supply-chain services Public-health analysis Data and analytics Monitoring and evaluation Independent evaluation Research Strategy development Organizational consulting Finance and accounting services Audit and assurance Risk management Information technology Digital systems Communications Knowledge management Human resources consulting Legal or regulatory support Program management Project management Logistics Procurement of goods Health-product procurement Pharmaceutical products Diagnostic products Other specialized technical or operational services Actual eligibility and technical requirements are determined separately for each solicitation. Global Fund Consulting Opportunities Consultancy assignments represent an important component of the Global Fund s external contracting activities. The Global Fund s careers information confirms that it engages both individual consultants and consultancy firms , with relevant opportunities published through the Business Consultancy Opportunities section. These assignments should not be confused with permanent employment vacancies. Permanent and fixed-term staff vacancies generally appear through the Global Fund s separate careers system, while consulting and supplier procurements are normally handled as contracting opportunities. Consultants may therefore be engaged to deliver specific outputs, technical expertise, analysis, assessments, evaluations or other professional services under contractual terms defined in the relevant solicitation. Global Fund Procurement Opportunities for Suppliers Companies interested in doing business with the Global Fund should understand that procurement is governed by formal institutional rules. The Global Fund states that it seeks value for money in the procurement of goods and services and publishes tenders as part of a transparent procurement process. Its Procurement Policy applies to several areas, including: Procurement of health products and related services through the Pooled Procurement Mechanism. Procurement of goods and services financed through Global Fund operating expenses. Certain other procurements financed through approved investments or funds. Procurement of Local Fund Agent services. This means the procurement framework covers both operational requirements and major elements of the organization s health-product supply system. Open Competition Is the Standard Procurement Approach One of the most important aspects for prospective bidders is the Global Fund s emphasis on competitive procurement. Its Procurement Policy states that procurement should generally be based on effective competition and identifies open competition as the organization s standard procurement method. Effective competition may involve: Publicly advertising procurement opportunities; Inviting a sufficient number of prospective suppliers; Ensuring bidders compete under equivalent conditions; Receiving sufficient independent offers; and Evaluating proposals against established requirements. This approach is intended to provide a transparent and competitive environment for qualified suppliers. Core Global Fund Procurement Principles Prospective applicants should understand the principles against which Global Fund procurement is managed. 1. Value for Money Procurement decisions are not necessarily based solely on selecting the lowest-priced offer. The Global Fund defines value for money by considering the relationship among: Price Quality Performance Total cost of ownership Technical suitability Delivery requirements Organizational capability Environmental, social, sustainability and risk considerations may also be incorporated where relevant. A bidder should therefore ensure that its proposal demonstrates overall value rather than simply offering a low financial price. 2. Effective Competition Competitive procurement is intended to ensure multiple qualified suppliers have a fair opportunity to participate. The organization seeks an adequate competitive environment and normally uses open competition as its standard approach. 3. Fairness, Impartiality and Integrity The Global Fund requires bidders to be treated equally and proposals to be evaluated objectively against predetermined criteria. Its Procurement Policy specifically emphasizes avoiding actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. 4. Client-Centered Procurement Procurement is also expected to meet the requirements of the internal Global Fund unit requesting the goods or services. This means suppliers must closely understand the technical specifications and intended outcomes of each tender. 5. Sustainable Procurement The Global Fund explicitly incorporates sustainability into its procurement framework. Its policy states that sustainable procurement seeks to: Reduce environmental impacts across supply chains; Support fair and humane working conditions; Promote social progress; Support economic development; and Contribute to the long-term well-being of communities. 6. Best Interests of the Global Fund Procurement must ultimately support the organization s mission, protect its assets and ensure responsible stewardship of its resources. Ethical Requirements for Global Fund Suppliers Ethical compliance is a major requirement for companies and consultants seeking contracts with the organization. The Global Fund s Code of Conduct for Suppliers applies broadly to bidders, suppliers, agents, intermediaries, consultants and contractors, as well as relevant representatives, employees, subcontractors and affiliates. Suppliers are expected to participate in procurement processes honestly, fairly, transparently and accountably. The organization prohibits practices including: Corruption Fraud Collusion Anti-competitive practices Coercion Misrepresentation Improper payments Undisclosed commissions Other unethical procurement practices Applicants should therefore ensure that every statement, qualification, reference, financial proposal and declaration contained in their bid is accurate. Compliance With Laws Suppliers and their representatives are required to comply with applicable laws and regulations in the countries where they conduct business, as well as relevant Global Fund rules and policies. The Code of Conduct also includes provisions concerning matters such as: Anti-corruption Anti-money laundering Fair competition Responsible use of Global Fund resources Disclosure of conflicts Human rights Labor standards Environmental responsibilities Child protection Protection from sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment These requirements should be treated as substantive contractual obligations rather than formalities. Record-Keeping and Audit Requirements Companies that obtain Global Fund-financed contracts should also be prepared for accountability and audit requirements. The Supplier Code of Conduct requires suppliers to maintain appropriate and complete financial and business records associated with Global Fund-financed contracts for at least five years after the final payment under the contract . Suppliers are also expected to cooperate with the Global Fund, including its Office of the Inspector General , where access to relevant records, documents or personnel is reasonably requested. This requirement is particularly relevant to larger consulting firms, contractors and suppliers managing financially significant contracts. Conflicts of Interest Potential suppliers must pay close attention to conflict-of-interest requirements. The procurement framework seeks to ensure objective evaluation and prevent circumstances where a bidder could obtain an improper competitive advantage. Suppliers should disclose relevant relationships or situations where required and carefully review the specific tender documentation before submitting their proposal. Failure to properly address conflicts may jeopardize a bid or contract. Can Suppliers Use the Global Fund Name or Logo? Winning a Global Fund contract does not automatically authorize a supplier to use the organization s name or logo for advertising. The Supplier Code states that suppliers may not, without prior written consent, use the Global Fund s name or logo in publicity or advertising, represent a business relationship as an endorsement of their products or services, or make statements on behalf of the Global Fund. Companies should therefore obtain appropriate authorization before publicly promoting a contractual relationship. Health Product Procurement Opportunities The Global Fund is also a major procurer of medicines and health products. Its Pooled Procurement Mechanism (PPM) aggregates orders from participating grant implementers to obtain competitive prices and delivery conditions from manufacturers and suppliers. In 2025, the mechanism handled approximately US$1.02 billion in orders for implementing partners in 81 countries . Products available through the mechanism include categories such as: Antiretroviral medicines Antimalarial medicines Other essential medicines Insecticide-treated mosquito nets Viral load tests Rapid diagnostic tests Regular tenders for medicines and diagnostic products may also appear through the Business Consultancy Opportunities section. Important Information for Health Product Suppliers Companies interested specifically in supplying medicines or health products should not rely exclusively on the general tender page. The Global Fund advises potential health-product suppliers to: Review its Procurement Policy. Understand quality-assurance requirements applicable to their products. Review relevant procurement and purchasing information. Understand the Pooled Procurement Mechanism and wambo.org. Review the Code of Conduct for Suppliers. Review applicable procurement regulations. The organization does not maintain a general list of automatically preselected suppliers for implementing partners. Manufacturers must therefore satisfy the particular regulatory, quality and procurement conditions applicable to their products. What Documents Should Applicants Read Before Applying? The Global Fund explicitly advises prospective bidders to review key procurement documentation before submitting a proposal. Important documents include: Procurement Policy Code of Conduct for Suppliers Terms and Conditions for the Purchase of Goods and Services Privacy Statement for the Global Fund Procurement Process Travel Guidelines for Contractors Applicants should not treat these documents as optional background reading. They can establish important conditions relating to: Ethical conduct Contract administration Financial arrangements Confidentiality Travel Compliance Reporting Supplier obligations Legal liability Tender-specific conditions may supplement these general rules. How to Apply for Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities The application procedure is not identical for every procurement. The official Business Consultancy Opportunities page directs applicants to the Global Fund s Open Tenders platform. Each individual solicitation contains its own: Tender description Terms of reference or specifications Eligibility requirements Required qualifications Submission procedure Technical documentation Financial requirements Deadline Contact or clarification procedure Applicants should therefore first identify a tender that matches their qualifications and carefully review the complete tender package before preparing a proposal. View Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities Preparing a Competitive Proposal Although tender requirements vary, applicants should generally prepare to demonstrate why they are technically and commercially capable of delivering the requested work. A strong proposal may need to address areas such as: Understanding of the Assignment Demonstrate a clear understanding of: The Global Fund s requirements Expected outputs Relevant technical issues Contract objectives Deliverables Technical Approach Where required, explain: Proposed methodology Implementation approach Work plan Quality-assurance arrangements Risk management Project governance Reporting arrangements Relevant Experience Applicants may need to demonstrate previous experience delivering similar assignments. Evidence could include: Comparable contracts Client references Case studies Project summaries Past performance Demonstrated international experience Personnel Consultancy tenders may require CVs of proposed experts. Applicants should ensure that each proposed team member clearly satisfies any mandatory: Education requirements Professional qualifications Years of experience Technical competencies Language requirements Financial Proposal Price should be realistic and consistent with the technical methodology. Because Global Fund procurement evaluates overall value for money rather than price alone, applicants should avoid compromising technical quality merely to submit the lowest possible price. Evaluation of Proposals The exact scoring methodology will be provided in the individual tender documentation. However, the Global Fund s overarching Procurement Policy permits consideration of: Technical factors Commercial factors Organizational factors Pricing Environmental factors Social considerations Sustainability Risk Appropriate due diligence Applicants should therefore respond directly to every evaluation criterion instead of submitting a generic corporate proposal. Tender Review and Contract Award The Global Fund s procurement framework includes controls before contracts are awarded. Its Procurement Policy states that procurement contracts are subject to a mandatory review process prior to award to confirm compliance with applicable policies and procurement rules. No award may be made before that review is completed. This reflects the organization s emphasis on transparency, accountability and procurement integrity. Are These Opportunities Based in Geneva? Many opportunities published through this particular portal primarily involve supplying goods or services to the Global Fund Secretariat in Geneva, Switzerland . However, this does not necessarily mean every consultant must permanently reside in Switzerland. Assignment location, travel requirements, remote-working arrangements and geographical eligibility can differ substantially from one tender to another. Applicants should therefore consult the individual Terms of Reference rather than assuming an opportunity is either remote or Geneva-based. Can International Applicants Apply? The Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities page does not establish one universal nationality restriction covering all tenders . It states that open tenders are available for prospective suppliers to review and consider. The Supplier Code also covers a broad range of bidders, suppliers, consultants, contractors, organizations and representatives. However, international eligibility must be determined tender by tender . A specific procurement may impose requirements relating to: Country registration Geographic presence Local expertise Language Tax registration Professional licensing Experience in certain regions Ability to travel Manufacturer authorization Product regulatory approval Applicants should therefore never interpret the general procurement page as guaranteeing eligibility for every nationality in every procurement. Are There Opportunities for Applicants From Africa, Asia, Europe and Other Regions? Potentially, yes, depending on the specific tender. The Global Fund operates globally, and its procurement ecosystem includes international companies, consultants, manufacturers and service providers. But there is no blanket statement on the Business Consultancy Opportunities page saying every tender is universally open to every country . Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Oceania should check the nationality, registration and location provisions of each individual procurement notice. Application Deadline There is no single overall deadline for Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities. This is an ongoing procurement portal. Each open tender has its own closing date and submission time , which are stated within the individual solicitation documentation. The official page specifically directs applicants to the individual tender for submission instructions and contact information. Applicants should therefore: Open the current tender list. Identify the relevant opportunity. Check its exact closing date. Note the applicable time zone. Submit the complete proposal before the stated deadline. Late submissions may not be accepted under tender-specific rules. Important Difference Between Global Fund Tenders and Global Fund Jobs Applicants should understand that this procurement portal is not the Global Fund s ordinary employment vacancies page . The organization maintains a separate recruitment system for staff vacancies. Its careers page specifically explains that consulting opportunities for consultants and consultancy firms are listed under Business Consultancy Opportunities. Therefore: Permanent or temporary employment: Check Global Fund Careers. Consultancy contracts, supplier opportunities and tenders: Check Business Consultancy Opportunities. This distinction is particularly important for applicants preparing CVs or proposals. Why Consider Global Fund Business Opportunities? Working with the Global Fund can provide experienced consultants and organizations with an opportunity to contribute specialized expertise to one of the world s major global health financing institutions. Potential benefits include: Participation in international health initiatives Exposure to complex global programs Opportunities to work with international stakeholders Experience with major institutional procurement systems Potential long-term professional relationships Opportunities for specialist consulting firms Participation in health-product and supply-chain initiatives Work contributing indirectly to the fight against HIV, tuberculosis and malaria However, applicants should approach these opportunities as formal competitive procurements rather than guaranteed contracts. Tips for Prospective Applicants Before submitting a Global Fund tender, applicants should: Read the complete Terms of Reference or technical specifications. Confirm that all mandatory eligibility criteria can be satisfied. Read the Procurement Policy. Review the Supplier Code of Conduct. Examine the applicable Terms and Conditions. Prepare a proposal specifically tailored to the tender. Demonstrate relevant experience with evidence. Provide qualified personnel where required. Address every evaluation criterion. Ensure pricing is complete and commercially realistic. Disclose potential conflicts where required. Avoid unsupported claims about organizational capacity. Confirm the deadline and applicable time zone. Submit through the method specified in the tender. Retain copies of all documents submitted. Important Warning for Applicants Applicants should use only official Global Fund procurement channels and verify all tender information against the official website. A legitimate procurement process should include formal documentation defining the required goods or services, submission requirements and applicable conditions. Prospective bidders should also remember that winning a Global Fund contract does not provide unrestricted permission to use the organization s name or logo for advertising purposes. Conclusion The Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities platform provides an important route for qualified consultants, businesses, manufacturers, contractors and professional service providers seeking to work with an internationally recognized global health financing organization. Unlike a conventional job board, the platform operates as an ongoing competitive procurement system , with individual tenders covering different goods, consulting assignments and specialized services. The Global Fund emphasizes transparency, effective competition, integrity, sustainability and value for money throughout its procurement activities. Applicants should therefore expect rigorous technical, ethical and contractual standards. There is no universal application deadline . Each opportunity has its own closing date, technical requirements, financial requirements and submission procedure. Prospective suppliers and consultants should regularly review the official portal, identify opportunities aligned with their expertise, carefully study all tender documentation and prepare compliant, evidence-based proposals. title: USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program in Washington, D.C.: Applications Open for U.S. Citizens Interested in Public Service, Agriculture, Policy and Rural Development
summary: Applications are now open for the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Spring 2027 Internship Program , offering emerging professionals an opportunity to gain practical experience inside one of the largest departments of the U.S. federal government. The Spring 2027 cohort will run from January 25 through April 30, 2027 , with applications due by November 13, 2026 . The program is an unpaid, in-person volunteer internship based in Washington, D.C. USDA does not provide housing or relocation assistance. Unlike many internships that are limited to currently enrolled university students, USDA s current Internship Program does not require applicants to be enrolled in school or to hold a college degree . According to USDA s official FAQ, applicants must be U.S. citizens and at least 18 years old at the time of application . Candidates from a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds may therefore be considered. The program provides participants with direct exposure to public service and federal government operations while allowing them to contribute to work related to agriculture, food systems, conservation, rural communities, communications, research, public policy, stakeholder engagement and other areas central to USDA s mission. About the USDA Internship Program The U.S. Department of Agriculture describes its Internship Program as a public-service and leadership-development experience intended to introduce emerging leaders to USDA s work and help prepare them for careers in public service, agriculture, science, policy and community development. USDA s mission reaches far beyond farming alone. The Department works across areas including: Agriculture and agricultural markets Food and nutrition Food safety Rural economic development Natural-resource conservation Forestry and environmental stewardship Agricultural research Data and economics International agricultural trade Communications Public policy Congressional relations Civil rights Community partnerships Stakeholder engagement Interns may therefore have opportunities to work in areas aligned with a broad range of academic interests, professional skills and career ambitions. USDA states that interns may contribute to activities such as research, program operations, data analysis, communications, outreach and stakeholder engagement. Exact responsibilities depend on the mission area or staff office in which an intern is placed. Spring 2027 USDA Internship Dates The current application is specifically for the Spring 2027 cohort . Program period: January 25, 2027 – April 30, 2027 Application deadline: November 13, 2026 USDA s application information states that applicants should be available during the program period. The application form itself also allows candidates with limited availability to explain their circumstances, although applicants should expect the program to require substantial in-person participation. Applicants should therefore carefully consider academic, employment, transportation and housing commitments before applying. Is the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Paid? No. The current USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program is explicitly described as an unpaid volunteer internship . Applicants will not receive a salary from USDA through this program. This distinction is important because USDA also operates other student employment initiatives, including Pathways opportunities, some of which may be paid. The internship advertised on the USDA page linked above, however, is the USDA Volunteer Internship Program and is unpaid. USDA encourages applicants to explore whether their educational institutions or relevant nonprofit organizations can provide funding or academic support. Applicants should also be aware that outside income, funding or housing assistance associated with the internship may require prior approval from USDA. Housing and Relocation Assistance USDA does not provide housing specifically for interns under this program. Participants are responsible for finding and paying for their own accommodation for the duration of the internship. USDA also states on the Spring 2027 application page that the program provides no housing or relocation assistance . Candidates who do not already live within commuting distance of Washington, D.C., should therefore calculate expected costs before accepting an internship, including: Housing Transportation Meals Local commuting Relocation expenses Personal living expenses Because the position is unpaid, financial planning will be particularly important for applicants relocating to Washington. Internship Location: Washington, D.C. The USDA Internship Program is conducted in person in Washington, D.C. Interns are expected to work onsite at USDA s Whitten Building , where they participate directly in departmental operations and interact with USDA personnel. USDA specifically states that remote participation is not available for this program. Applicants should therefore not apply on the assumption that they will be permitted to complete the internship remotely from another U.S. state or another country. Expected Internship Schedule and Working Hours Most USDA internships under this program operate on a Monday-to-Friday schedule , typically within approximately 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Some flexibility may be available for interns who have academic or other program requirements. USDA states that interns considered full-time are generally expected to work the equivalent of approximately 4.5 days per week , although limited adjustments may be permitted where appropriate. Applicants should therefore view the opportunity as a substantial professional commitment rather than a few-hours-per-week volunteer placement. What Will USDA Interns Do? Specific duties will depend heavily on the intern s assigned mission area or staff office. USDA identifies potential internship activities including: Conducting research Supporting program operations Analyzing data Drafting communications Assisting with outreach activities Supporting stakeholder engagement Developing briefing materials Supporting meetings and events Conducting policy-related research Helping coordinate projects Participating in departmental programming This structure allows interns to gain practical experience while contributing to ongoing federal government activities. Leadership and Professional Development The program is not intended to consist solely of administrative assignments. USDA describes it as a leadership-development and public-service experience designed to help young and emerging professionals better understand federal service. Interns participate in department-wide programming, including lunch-and-learn sessions featuring USDA leaders and subject-matter experts . Through these activities, interns may gain exposure to: Federal decision-making Government leadership Agriculture and food policy Public administration Interagency operations Stakeholder engagement Professional networking Career development Public-service culture USDA Mission Areas and Offices Available to Applicants As part of the application, candidates must list their top three preferred USDA Mission Areas or Staff Offices . USDA s official Office Opportunities document identifies a wide range of potential placement areas. 1. Farm Production and Conservation Farm Production and Conservation (FPAC) serves as a major focal point for farmers, ranchers and other stewards of private agricultural and forest lands. Its work includes programs related to: Crop insurance Agricultural conservation Farm safety nets Lending Disaster programs Risk mitigation for agricultural producers This area may be particularly relevant for applicants interested in agricultural economics, environmental policy, farming systems, risk management or public administration. 2. Food and Nutrition Administration The Food and Nutrition Administration focuses on reducing food insecurity and improving nutrition security in the United States. Its work includes administration of federal domestic nutrition-assistance programs as well as science-based nutrition guidance, policy coordination and nutrition education. This area may appeal to applicants interested in food security, nutrition, social policy, public health or program management. 3. Food Safety and Inspection Service The Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is USDA s public-health agency responsible for helping ensure the safety of meat, poultry and egg products. Its work includes food-safety oversight and implementation of federal laws governing meat, poultry, egg products and humane animal handling. Students and professionals interested in food science, public health, veterinary science, regulatory policy or compliance may find this mission area particularly relevant. 4. Marketing and Regulatory Programs Marketing and Regulatory Programs (MRP) supports domestic and international agricultural markets while protecting U.S. plant and animal health. Its responsibilities include: Agricultural marketing Plant health Animal health Biotechnology regulation Animal-welfare administration Wildlife-damage management Participation in national and international standards development 5. Research, Education and Economics The Research, Education and Economics (REE) mission area supports research, analysis and education related to a safe, competitive and sustainable U.S. food and agricultural system. Its work also addresses communities, families and young people. Applicants interested in science, statistics, economics, research, data analysis or education may find REE especially relevant. 6. Rural Development USDA Rural Development supports rural communities through loans, grants and loan-guarantee programs. Its work includes investments relating to: High-speed internet Electricity Transportation infrastructure Businesses Healthcare Education Housing Community facilities This placement could be highly relevant for students of economics, finance, infrastructure, public policy, community development or business administration. 7. Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs (TFAA) works to expand international opportunities for American farmers and ranchers. Its responsibilities include international agricultural trade policy, market intelligence, trade promotion and export development. USDA s Foreign Agricultural Service maintains a global network covering numerous countries, while the U.S. Codex Office coordinates American participation in international food-standard setting. This area may be particularly attractive to applicants interested in international relations, economics, trade, diplomacy, agriculture or global food policy. 8. Natural Resources and Environment The Natural Resources and Environment (NRE) mission area focuses on maintaining the health, diversity and productivity of U.S. forests and grasslands. It works with states, tribes and communities across the country to steward natural resources. Applicants with interests in environmental studies, forestry, climate policy, conservation, sustainability or natural-resource management may consider this placement. USDA Staff Offices Offering Internship Exposure Applicants can also express preferences for USDA staff offices. Office of the Secretary The Office of the Secretary provides leadership and strategic direction across USDA. Interns may support: High-level policy coordination Research Briefing materials Departmental decision-making Senior leadership meetings Major events This placement provides particularly close exposure to senior-level federal policy and executive decision-making. White House Liaison Office The White House Liaison Office connects USDA with the Executive Office of the President. Its responsibilities include personnel matters, political appointments, leadership onboarding and coordination with the White House. Interns may assist with research, personnel processes, organizational analysis, briefings and leadership engagements. Office of Communications The Office of Communications manages public information and strategic communication across USDA. Internship work may involve: Writing and editing Press support Briefing materials Digital content Media monitoring Event support Visual storytelling Strategic messaging It may be particularly suitable for applicants interested in journalism, public relations, communications, digital media or public affairs. Office of Congressional Relations The Office of Congressional Relations acts as USDA s main liaison with the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate. Interns may gain experience in: Legislative research Tracking congressional hearings Monitoring legislation Preparing background materials Congressional communications Supporting departmental engagements with lawmakers Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights The Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR) leads USDA s work relating to civil-rights compliance and equal treatment. Potential intern activities include: Civil-rights policy research Data analysis Training-material preparation Outreach Compliance-related work Office of Partnerships and Public Engagement The Office of Partnerships and Public Engagement (OPPE) works with rural and underserved communities and helps connect stakeholders with USDA programs and resources. Interns may assist with: Outreach strategy Partnership development Community-needs research Event coordination Stakeholder engagement materials Who Can Apply? One of the distinctive features of the current USDA internship is its relatively broad educational eligibility. According to USDA: Applicants must be at least 18 years old . Applicants must be U.S. citizens . Applicants do not need to be currently enrolled in school. Applicants do not need to hold a college degree. People from a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds may apply. The online application provides education-status options including: Currently enrolled in high school Currently enrolled in college or university Recently graduated Not currently enrolled in school This confirms that the program is not restricted solely to university students. Does an Applicant Need a Specific Major? No specific academic major is identified as a universal requirement for the program. The application nevertheless asks candidates to identify their major or field of study , where applicable. Applicants who are not currently enrolled may provide their most recent field of study or indicate that the question is not applicable. Given USDA s broad responsibilities, potentially relevant backgrounds include—but are not limited to: Agriculture Agricultural economics Economics Finance Business administration Public administration Public policy Political science International relations Law Communications Journalism Data science Statistics Computer science Food science Nutrition Public health Environmental science Forestry Biology Animal sciences Rural development Sociology Community development Applicants should choose office preferences that align logically with their interests, abilities and professional goals. Is a Minimum GPA Required? The application asks candidates to provide a GPA, but USDA marks the GPA field as optional . The current program page therefore does not establish a universal minimum GPA requirement for the Spring 2027 Volunteer Internship Program. USDA Internship Application Requirements The application must be submitted through USDA s official online portal. Hard-copy applications sent by mail are not accepted . Applicants will need to complete several sections. Section 1: Personal Information Applicants provide details including: Full name Street address City, state and ZIP code Telephone number Email address Section 2: Education Applicants indicate their education status and provide applicable details such as: Current school or university Major or field of study Expected graduation date GPA, if they choose to provide it Section 3: Spring 2027 Availability Applicants must indicate whether they are available for the full Spring 2027 semester or have limited availability. Candidates selecting limited availability must provide an explanation. Section 4: Statement of Interest The application requires substantive written responses addressing several topics. Applicants are asked to explain: Why they are interested in an internship with USDA. What skills and experiences they could bring to USDA. Which issues affecting agriculture, food systems, conservation or rural communities they want to learn more about and why. What public service means to them and how they have demonstrated commitment to their community. A personal accomplishment they are proud of and how it shaped their perspective on success. The application also asks whether applicants have previously volunteered or worked for a: Political campaign Elected official Government official Applicants answering yes are asked to describe their role and the relevant campaign, office or official as well as the year or years involved. Importantly, USDA states separately that political preference is not used as a deciding factor in internship application review . Section 5: Office Preferences Candidates must identify their top three USDA Mission Areas or Staff Offices where they would prefer to intern. Applicants should research these offices before selecting preferences because their choices can help communicate their career interests and indicate where their skills may best fit USDA s needs. Section 6: References Applicants must provide at least two references who can discuss their: Qualifications Character Work ethic Commitment to public service USDA suggests potential references such as: Professors Supervisors Mentors Community leaders Applicants should provide complete contact information for each reference. Recommendation letters are optional and may be uploaded as PDF documents if applicants wish to include them. All required reference information must be submitted by the application deadline. USDA notes that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , which makes early submission advisable. Resume Requirement Applicants must upload a resume. The application portal currently accepts: PDF DOC DOCX The maximum upload size shown on the application form is 20 MB . Candidates should tailor their resume to demonstrate relevant experience rather than using a generic resume whenever possible. Useful information may include: Education Work experience Volunteer experience Leadership activities Community involvement Research projects Public-service activities Relevant technical skills Communication skills Data or analytical experience Policy experience Agriculture, food or environmental interests How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application Because the program seeks individuals interested in public service, candidates should demonstrate more than academic achievement alone. Strong applications should provide concrete evidence of: Interest in USDA s mission Commitment to public service Community involvement Leadership Initiative Research or analytical skills Communication ability Professional maturity Interest in agriculture, food systems, conservation or rural communities When answering the statement-of-interest questions, applicants should avoid vague claims such as I am passionate about agriculture. Instead, they should explain why a particular issue matters to them, what they have already done in that area, what they hope to learn and how USDA experience fits their longer-term professional objectives. Political Experience and Political Preference Applicants are specifically asked whether they have worked or volunteered for a political campaign, elected official or government official. However, USDA states that political preference itself is not considered in the application review process . Applicants should answer the application questions accurately and transparently. What matters is their ability to demonstrate commitment to USDA s public-service mission and responsibilities toward farmers, rural communities and the American public. Important Financial Considerations Before Applying Because the Spring 2027 internship is unpaid and based in Washington, D.C., candidates should evaluate the financial implications carefully. Before applying or accepting an offer, consider: Whether you can live in or commute to Washington, D.C., from January through April 2027. Whether your college or university can provide academic credit or financial assistance. Whether you qualify for support from an external nonprofit organization. Your housing costs. Transportation and commuting costs. Food and personal expenses. Whether outside funding would require USDA approval. The absence of compensation does not diminish the professional exposure available through the program, but applicants should make a realistic financial assessment before committing. Why Consider the USDA Spring 2027 Internship? The program may be particularly valuable for individuals interested in understanding how federal institutions operate in practice. Participants may gain firsthand exposure to: Federal public administration Agricultural policymaking Policy research Data analysis Rural-development programs Food and nutrition programs Environmental conservation International agricultural trade Congressional relations Communications Civil-rights compliance Community engagement Executive-branch operations Because internship placements span both policy-focused and operational offices, the program can be relevant to candidates from many academic and professional backgrounds. The experience may also help applicants determine whether a longer-term career in public service, agriculture, federal policy or related sectors is appropriate for them. Application Deadline The official deadline for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program is November 13, 2026 . USDA notes that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so interested candidates should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their materials. How to Apply for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Applications must be submitted electronically through the official USDA Internship Application portal. Apply for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Applicants can review the main program information here: USDA Internship Program Official Website Before submitting, candidates should make sure they have: Completed all personal and educational information. Confirmed their Spring 2027 availability. Prepared strong responses to the statement-of-interest questions. Selected three preferred USDA mission areas or offices. Provided two appropriate references with current contact information. Prepared an updated resume. Uploaded any optional recommendation letters they wish to include. title: GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship 2026–2027: Global Opportunity for Education System Leaders to Transform Education at Scale
summary: The GIFTS – Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems is a new global fellowship designed for influential education system leaders who are working to reshape education systems and create better futures for children and young people. What Is the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship? GIFTS stands for the Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems . Economic developments, technological advances and climate-related changes are creating new challenges and opportunities for education. At the same time, education systems are expected to ensure that children and young people develop not only academic capabilities but also the purpose and agency required to navigate an uncertain future. The fellowship recognises that education-system leaders play a critical role in responding to these changes. These leaders are expected to: Chart new paths for their education systems. Adapt institutions and strategies to changing realities. Improve the performance of complex systems. Mobilise people at different levels of the education system. Inspire students, teachers and school leaders. Work with government and other partners. Address difficult system-level challenges. Develop strategies capable of producing sustainable change. Despite the importance and complexity of this work, education-system leaders may have relatively few opportunities to connect with peers, reflect on their experiences and share practical lessons about what it takes to transform education systems. The fellowship will encourage participants to investigate fundamental questions about education-system transformation. title: DA Young Leaders Programme 2027: Applications Open for Young South Africans Interested in Political and Public Service Leadership
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Democratic Alliance (DA) Young Leaders Programme (YLP) , a one-year political leadership learning and development programme designed for young South Africans who are passionate about leadership, public service, politics and creating positive change in their communities. The programme provides an opportunity for motivated young people to strengthen their political knowledge, critical-thinking abilities, communication skills and personal leadership capabilities while gaining practical experience through a dedicated leadership project. For young South Africans considering a future in politics, government, public service or community leadership, the DA Young Leaders Programme offers structured leadership development designed to help participants understand their leadership potential, identify areas for personal growth, and develop the skills required to become effective changemakers. About the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027 The DA Young Leaders Programme is described as a political leadership learning and development programme for South Africans aged between 18 and 35 who align themselves with the Democratic Alliance s values of Freedom, Fairness, Opportunity and Diversity . The programme is aimed at highly motivated individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in politics or the public service and who want to contribute to building what the DA describes as One Nation with One Future. Rather than focusing only on theoretical leadership concepts, the programme combines political learning, personal development, communication development and practical leadership experience. Participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of politics while also gaining greater insight into their own leadership style, strengths and development needs. Over the course of one year, Young Leaders participate in activities intended to broaden their political knowledge and critical-thinking capabilities. They also develop communication skills and take part in dedicated sessions focused on leadership and personal development. A central component of the programme is the requirement for each participant to conceptualise and undertake a leadership project . This gives participants an opportunity to apply what they learn in a practical setting while addressing an issue within their community. Who Should Apply for the DA Young Leaders Programme? The programme is designed for young people who are not only interested in leadership but are already demonstrating a commitment to making a positive difference in their communities. According to the programme information, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate qualities such as Integrity and a strong commitment to serving others. Leadership potential and motivation to create meaningful change. A desire to continue developing their personal and professional potential. An interest in politics, public service or government as a potential career path. A passion for contributing to a better future for South Africa. The ability to align their personal values with the Democratic Alliance s liberal values and principles. An interest in strengthening their critical-thinking, communication, writing, public-speaking, and leadership skills. The programme therefore goes beyond identifying young people who simply have an interest in politics. It seeks individuals who demonstrate leadership potential, community commitment and a willingness to take responsibility for creating meaningful change. What Participants Can Gain from the Young Leaders Programme The DA Young Leaders Programme provides a combination of political education, leadership development, personal development and practical experience. 1. Political Knowledge and Understanding Participants have the opportunity to broaden their understanding of politics and develop greater political knowledge. This can help them better understand the issues affecting South Africa and the role that effective leadership can play in addressing national and community challenges. The political learning component is particularly relevant for young people considering future careers in political leadership, government or public service. 2. Critical-Thinking Skills Critical thinking is another important area of development within the programme. Participants are challenged to think critically and develop the ability to engage with issues in a thoughtful and informed manner. These skills can be valuable for people interested in policy, public leadership, government and community development. 3. Communication Development Communication is a major component of effective leadership, and the programme provides participants with opportunities to strengthen their communication abilities. Participants are expected to develop their: Writing skills Public-speaking abilities General communication skills Ability to express ideas effectively Capacity to engage with political and community issues These skills can be particularly valuable for aspiring public representatives and future leaders. 4. Personal Leadership Development The programme also places considerable emphasis on personal development. Participants are given opportunities to understand themselves better, including their individual leadership styles and areas where they need further development. Dedicated leadership and personal-development sessions are intended to support this process. This emphasis means that the programme is not solely focused on external leadership responsibilities. It also encourages participants to develop self-awareness and understand how their individual characteristics can influence the way they lead. 5. Practical Leadership Experience One of the distinguishing elements of the programme is the leadership project that every participant is required to undertake. Through this project, participants are able to move beyond classroom or theoretical learning and apply their leadership skills to a real-world challenge. The programme states that these projects provide experience in areas such as: Planning Collaboration Community engagement Leadership Problem-solving Public leadership This practical experience can help participants build confidence and develop a stronger understanding of what effective leadership looks like in real communities. Leadership in Action: The Programme s Community Projects The leadership project component is intended to create meaningful impact within participants communities. According to the programme information, previous projects have addressed a range of social and community challenges. Examples provided by the programme include initiatives focused on gender-based violence awareness, school support, youth employment, housing and education. Examples include: Anti-Gender-Based Violence Awareness Some Young Leaders have developed campaigns focused on raising awareness about gender-based violence. These initiatives have included empowering young women and organising public gatherings against gender-based violence. Such projects demonstrate how leadership development can be connected to advocacy and community mobilisation. School Support Initiatives Other projects have focused on supporting disadvantaged schoolchildren. The examples include initiatives that provided children with essential items such as proper shoes, with the broader aim of supporting their confidence and sense of pride. Female Youth Employment Projects Some participants have worked on projects designed to address youth employment challenges among disadvantaged girls. These initiatives have sought to help bridge the gap between secondary education and full-time employment, demonstrating how Young Leaders can use community projects to address barriers facing young people. Housing and Education Projects Other leadership projects have addressed housing and community resilience. The programme highlights projects involving the construction of houses in vulnerable areas of the Western Cape, alongside efforts to educate local communities about the use of sandbag systems for flood protection. These examples illustrate the practical dimension of the Young Leaders Programme: participants are expected to use their leadership skills to engage with genuine challenges and develop initiatives that can produce tangible community benefits. The DA Young Leaders Programme s Long-Term Impact The Young Leaders Programme has already developed a substantial alumni network. According to the programme s information, more than 330 graduates have completed the programme since its launch. These alumni are described as making an impact across South Africa in public office, within the Democratic Alliance and through community initiatives. The programme reports the following impact figures: 330+ graduates have completed the Young Leaders Programme. 84 alumni are currently serving in public office, including as Members of Parliament, Members of Provincial Legislatures, councillors and other elected representatives. 7 members of the Democratic Alliance s leadership are alumni of the Young Leaders Programme. Alumni continue to contribute through community initiatives, public service and policy development across South Africa. These figures demonstrate the programme s stated role in developing a pipeline of young people who can go on to participate in political leadership, public service and community development. The Programme s Vision for South Africa The Young Leaders Programme is connected to the DA s broader vision for South Africa. The programme s stated vision is for a South Africa in which individuals have the opportunity to live lives that they value. It describes a country characterised by a dynamic and innovative society, an inclusive and growing economy, and a capable government that protects the Constitution and promotes equal opportunity. The vision emphasises equal opportunity regardless of where people are born, how they look or other arbitrary characteristics. The programme argues that achieving such a vision requires excellent leaders who are prepared to step forward and lead. Consequently, the Young Leaders Programme is positioned as part of the effort to prepare young South Africans for future leadership responsibilities. Applicants in either situation should therefore consult the official programme information or contact the YLP Office for clarification. What Makes the Programme Relevant to Aspiring Public Leaders? Leadership in politics and public service requires more than an interest in public affairs. Effective leaders need to communicate ideas, understand complex issues, work with others, engage communities and develop the confidence to make decisions. The Young Leaders Programme brings these areas together through political learning, critical thinking, communication development, personal leadership sessions and practical community projects. For young people considering a future in political or public leadership, the programme can therefore provide a structured environment in which to explore leadership ambitions while developing practical skills. Its emphasis on leadership projects is particularly significant because participants are expected to translate their learning into action. Rather than limiting leadership development to discussions and training sessions, the programme provides an opportunity to work on a real community challenge. Why Community Leadership Experience Matters The programme s emphasis on community projects reflects the importance of practical experience in leadership development. Working on a community initiative can require a participant to identify a problem, understand the people affected, develop an approach, work with others and implement activities. Such an experience can strengthen a range of leadership capabilities. The examples provided by the programme show that leadership projects can cover diverse areas, including social justice, education, employment, housing, gender-based violence awareness and community resilience. This provides participants with an opportunity to connect leadership development with issues that affect communities directly. title: Funded traineeships for young graduates at the EU Delegation to the United States – Apply by 14 September
summary: Are you a young graduate interested in international relations, diplomacy, European affairs, politics, communications, environment, economics or public policy ? The European Union Delegation to the United States is offering funded traineeships for young graduates across several sections of its Washington, D.C. delegation. The traineeships can last up to six months , with the tentative start date set for November 2026 , subject to budget availability. Application deadline: 14 September 2026. EU Delegation USA Funded Traineeships 2026 – Quick Overview Opportunity Details Host organisation EU Delegation to the United States Location United States of America Duration Up to 6 months Tentative start November 2026 Category Traineeship Funding Monthly grant Deadline 14 September 2026 Eligibility Young graduates with at least a Bachelor s degree Language Excellent English Work schedule Full-time, Monday–Friday Are you a young graduate interested in international relations? What is offered: Traineeships of up to 6 months within the following sections of the EU Delegation to the United States, subject to availability of the budget. The tentative start date is November 2026. Traineeship in the Administration Section (ADMIN): The Administration section provides support services to the Delegation staff, building, and residences. It encompasses Human Resources, Accounting Finance, Infrastructure, and Information Technology. It liaises with authorities in Europe and the United States on protocol and administrative matters related to EU officials. As a trainee in the Admin section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Support the logistical coordination and organization of meetings, events, workshops, and official visits, including escorting visitors to the Delegation. Receive, organize, and maintain office stationery, supplies, and other materials. Maintain accurate records of suppliers, orders, deliveries, and expenditures. Provide general administrative and clerical support to the Section, including filing, correspondence, scheduling, and document management. Attend internal and external meetings and prepare minutes, action points, and follow-up records. Assist with maintaining organized records and ensuring that administrative activities are completed efficiently and on time. Assist with market surveys Traineeship in the Global Issues and Innovation section (GIN): The Global Issues and Innovation section monitors and analyses U.S. political, economic, and regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety (which includes plant and animal health and animal welfare), public health, and consumer protection. As a trainee in the Global Issues and Innovation section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Researching U.S. regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, climate, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety, public health, and consumer protection. Attending U.S. Congressional hearings and other public events related to section policy areas and writing summaries for the section. Support the preparation of the Delegation’s outreach activities within the GIN section areas. Preparing minutes of section meetings. Traineeship in the Head of Delegation section (HOD): The Head of Delegation Section (HOD) supports the work of both the Ambassador and Deputy Ambassador in promoting positive relations with the United States. The HOD team coordinates with all Sections across the Delegation to establish priorities for the Ambassador’s agenda, ensure briefing for all scheduled meetings and engagements, coordinate a high number of social and diplomatic functions at the EU residence (dinners, lunches, receptions and events), and plan several State Outreach visits per year to build relationships at the State level with elected officials, business leaders and civil society. The HOD team also works with the wider Delegation to ensure the Ambassador’s participation in all high-level visits from Headquarters, and prepares the monthly coordination meetings of EU Ambassadors and Deputy Ambassadors as well as a monthly briefing call with EU Consuls General serving as EU Local Chairs around the US. The HOD intern will primarily be tasked to assist on State Outreach planning and events hosted by the Ambassador at the official EU Residence. As a trainee in the HOD section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: State Outreach: Conducting preliminary research to identify suitable meetings/events/partner in the destination State Assisting with pre-trip planning calls with contacts in the destination State Briefing assembly Post-trip follow-up correspondence Support to Social Secretary for Events at EU Residence Ad Hoc special projects at request of Ambassador Traineeship in the Political section (POL): The Political Section follows all aspects of the transatlantic agenda and closely monitors the work of Congress and the U.S. Administration on foreign, security, and defence policy, counterterrorism and home affairs, and human rights, as well as U.S. domestic policy and U.S. elections. The section maintains regular contact with a broad range of Washington-based NGOs, think tanks, and civil society organizations. As a trainee in the Political section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Attending virtual U.S. Congressional hearings and writing summaries. Attending think tank events and writing summaries of topics covered. Researching and writing reports on foreign policy, security, and development cooperation issues for the section. Contributing to briefings on issues related to the section’s priorities. Assisting with the organization of outreach events and activities related to political, security and development issues. Traineeship in the Press and Public Diplomacy section (PPD): The Press and Public Diplomacy section aims to highlight the work of the EU to various audiences in the U.S. As a horizontal section, PPD is the key coordinator of all the Delegation’s public outreach activities. The section is also responsible for the Delegation’s media relations and communications strategy. In addition, the section manages people-to-people initiatives and is in charge of the EU’s cultural diplomacy in the U.S. As a trainee in the Press and Public Diplomacy section, you will work on the following tasks: Main tasks: Assisting with the organization of public diplomacy events. Assisting with media monitoring and analysis and support for press events. Supporting the section with social media communication and digital content creation (website and social media). Monitoring events organized by think tanks and other organizations for reporting purposes. Providing research assistance as needed in areas related to the section s priorities. Preparing minutes of meetings and assisting with drafting briefings. Answering general information requests. Qualifications or special requirements : Must have at least a Bachelor s Diploma and background in relevant disciplines (International Affairs, European Affairs, Political Science, Law, Communications, Environment, Health, Science, Economics and other related policy areas). Excellent command of the English language. Be available full time, Monday through Friday. How to apply? Candidates must apply to the e-mail address delegation-usa-internships@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents: A detailed standard Europass curriculum vitae ( CV ) https://europa.eu/europass/en (CVs in other format will not be considered) a cover letter describing why you want to participate in a EU traineeship and an application form Please mention in the subject of your e-mail : Funded Traineeship ADMIN, GIN, HOD, POL, or PPD (you may only apply to 1 traineeship per delegation, however based on your profile, the delegation could offer you a traineeship in another section). Important information to read before applying Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship). Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee. Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected. The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. Citizens from EU Member states: must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation; must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation. title: DAAD University Summer Courses Scholarship 2027: Funded 4-Week German Language Programme With Accommodation, €475 Allowance and Travel Support
summary: Applications are open for the DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates , an international scholarship programme that enables eligible university students to spend four intensive weeks studying German language and regional studies at participating higher education institutions in Germany.
